decided.claim: Reveal rides the cross-desktop D-Bus org.freedesktop.FileManager1.ShowItems interface (Nautilus, Dolphin, Nemo, Caja, Thunar, PCManFM-Qt; D-Bus-activatable), called through whichever CLI is installed — gdbus, then dbus-send with the load-bearing --print-reply — instead of adding a dbus crate to a dependency-averse tree; if neither call succeeds, degrade to xdg-open on the containing directory.

path_to_file_uri percent-encodes everything outside unreserved + '/' so the URI's whole alphabet is inert in both CLIs' grammars (no comma for dbus-send's array to split on, nothing for gdbus's GVariant text to escape) — awkward filenames survive by construction, pinned by an encode/decode round-trip test.

file:// URIs decode via a hand-rolled strict-UTF-8 percent-decoder (malformed escapes kept literal, non-UTF-8 rejected): only an empty or localhost authority counts as this machine, ?query/#fragment are stripped, and the result is lexically normalised — no url crate.

link_under was split into a shared link_token_under plus a parallel reveal_path_under gate that returns Some only for an existing local item — a bare path resolved against the pane's cwd, or a decoded file:// URI — so web URLs, remote-host URIs, and dead paths never offer or attempt reveal.

The chord is modifiers.platform (Super) + control on left mouse-down, checked before the existing Shift/Ctrl open branch and falling through when nothing is revealable — so Shift-/Ctrl-click behaviour is untouched and Super+Ctrl on a web URL still opens it via the old branch.

reveal_with_system runs on a throwaway std::thread rather than open_with_system's detached setsid spawn, because choosing the fallback requires the D-Bus CLI's exit status (a wait of up to the bus timeout); the UI thread only spawns the thread, and the final fallback reuses the detached open_with_system.

The right-click menu row is hardcoded English ('Reveal in file manager  ⌖'), matching its untranslated neighbours ('Open link  ↗', 'Copy', 'Paste'), gated on reveal_path_under and shown alongside Open link when both apply.

The help modal's LINKS section documents the chord — k_super_ctrl_click/reveal_link added to the Strings struct and all nine language consts (my own translations) with the row wired in main.rs — and a CHANGELOG Unreleased/Added entry records the feature per the repo's keep-a-changelog convention.

least_confident.why: The gdbus/dbus-send invocations follow the canonical recipes (including gdbus's empty-string startup-id argument and both CLIs' nonzero exit on an unowned bus name), but I could not execute either; a parse quirk in gdbus's empty-arg handling would silently shift every reveal onto the dbus-send leg or the fallback.

Whether Super+Ctrl+click reaches the app at all depends on the compositor not grabbing Super chords (Hyprland's SUPER-drag binds match the exact modifier set so it should pass, but this is reasoning, not observation).
Eight of the nine help-modal translations are my own unreviewed wording; phrasing conventions for 'file manager' vary per locale.

not_done.claim: No build, test, or formatter run — cargo is out of scope for this exercise.
not_done.why: Everything is verified by reading only: compilation of all four files, the two new unit tests passing, and rustfmt conformance of the added blocks are unverified.

not_done.claim: reveal_path_under, the click routing, the menu row, and reveal_with_system's process behaviour are untested.
not_done.why: They need a live grid, a compositor, and a session bus; per the brief only the introduced pure logic (URI decode/encode, round-trip, inert alphabet) got tests.

not_done.claim: No busctl third attempt in the CLI chain.
not_done.why: gdbus (GLib) and dbus-send (dbus core) already cover any desktop that could own FileManager1; a box with neither still degrades to xdg-open of the parent directory rather than failing silently.

not_done.claim: ShowItems is passed an empty startup-notification id.
not_done.why: A real activation token would need platform plumbing; the cost is possible focus-stealing prevention leaving the file manager window unfocused on some desktops.

not_done.claim: Non-UTF-8 filesystem paths cannot be revealed from file:// URIs.
not_done.why: The decoder deliberately rejects them because the surrounding link plumbing is String-typed; a byte-preserving OsString path would be a larger refactor than the ticket warrants.
